Predicting connections in complex networks is crucial across multiple fields, 
including the study of molecular structures. Our approach utilizes knowledge 
retained by a neural network trained on a molecule's structural elements, 
enabling the prediction of its bonds through reverse engineering. We've 
developed SSNE, an efficient model that simulates a node's surroundings 
using a simplified representation of the entity itself and its connections to 
other points, discarding unnecessary information from the network. SSNE's 
performance surpasses current standards in accuracy and efficiency for 
large, intricate networks. It outperforms others in bond prediction tasks 
while using less computational power and storage. This research presents a 
novel understanding of molecular structure representation and opens doors for 
the study of various real-world complex systems. It also provides a resource 
for the analysis of network links in the context of the entity itself and its 
connections to other points, discarding unnecessary information from the 
network.

A novel atomic vapor chamber, employing nano-fabricated silicon diffusion chambers, is explored as a starting point for developing highly stable, on-chip atomic sensors with precise frequency stability. The featured silicon chip boasts an integrated "flower pot" chamber integrated into a silicon "pot" with a controlled depth and a "funnel" leading to a central collecting area, all fabricated using the 200mm angle-exposure DUV process. This silicon chip is paired with a holder featuring four gold wire loops for supporting the vapor chamber's base, as well as gold "feet" that securely attach the chip to a copper heat sink, ensuring efficient heat dissipation for regulating the vapor chamber's temperature. Using this setup, the achieved frequency stability ranges from 38 mHz to 121 mHz at various temperatures, as measured at atmospheric pressure. The best result, 38 mHz, is comparable to the stability obtained in a similar setup at reduced atmospheric pressure. This leading stability result showcases the capability of this arrangement to host the highest number of overlapping Fabry-Perot cavities, 11, as the silicon depth can be adjusted to achieve this configuration.

We develop a comprehensive model for calculating the nonlinear disruption distance of a dual-polarization 4D frequency-Intensity code. The model combines the interactions of second and third-order nonlinear processes to predict disruption performance accurately. Specifically, we leverage the second-order process to anticipate when the phase of the cross-polarized optical field will shift 180 degrees, while the third-order process governs intensity modulation. Causality is considered in the coupling equations for both processes. We experimentally validate the model by evaluating dual-polarization 4D frequency-intensity codes with varying complexity across multiple platforms. When precisely calculating the nonlinear disruption distance from the model, we achieve an average deviation of 0.05 $L_D$ (% relative deviation). Moreover, we demonstrate that the model enables straightforward design of PMF-based optical communication systems optimized for dual-polarization transmission, thereby opening up new possibilities for high-speed, error-free transmission over hundreds of meters.

Recent years have seen an alarming rise in wildfires and associated damage worldwide.
Consequently, enhancing wildfire detection, tracking, and forecasting has become a critical global priority.
Although significant progress has been made in developing AI capabilities for surveillance, satellite-based monitoring of wildfires remains a challenge due to inconsistent data quality and limited visual coverage.
In particular, infrared imaging provides crucial burn area information but is limited by its limited visibility range compared to visible imaging.
Thus, there's a pressing need to improve multi-spectral wildfire vision.
We propose an innovative approach, FIRe-GAN, for merging infrared and visible images of wildfires to produce high-quality, realistic multi-spectral data.
This novel technique leverages a generator and discriminator network, utilizing a patch-based feature loss to mimic the effects of combining infrared and visible images from wildfire scenes.
Our model outperforms current state-of-the-art image synthesis methods on multi-spectral wildfire data.
Moreover, incorporating FIRe-GAN with cutting-edge deep learning architectures significantly boosts the accuracy of detecting and tracking wildfires.

While indications of depression can be found in social media posts and discussions, the presence of irrelevant data necessitates an efficient method for categorizing and analyzing online content. To address this challenge, we collected and analyzed a large dataset from Instagram and Facebook, and employed statistical analysis to evaluate the correlation between social media interactions and depression indicators. Notably, our findings suggest that frequent social media engagement can be associated with certain depression symptoms, albeit with minimal certainty. However, further in-depth research is required to validate the findings and effectively utilize social media data to identify depression indicators and foster open discussions about mental health.

We've developed a novel statistical model for COVID-19, incorporating key non-pharmaceutical interventions such as mask wearing, social distancing, and personal hygiene measures. This multi-faceted approach treats the disease spread as a complex interplay of random factors influencing individual and group behaviors. Unlike traditional deterministic models, our random compartment model accounts for uncertainty in disease transmission and detection, as well as the probabilistic effect of contact between individuals and hospitalization of patients. Notably, its predictive capabilities align with the actual course of the pandemic in the US, closely estimating critical metrics such as peak incidence, mortality rates, and total deaths. To demonstrate its statistical efficacy, we show how to estimate model parameters by fitting the model to daily death count data using a likelihood-based approach. Furthermore, we employed the Varredor library for statistical analysis to showcase the model's performance in fitting and predicting COVID-19 outcomes in both the US and Brazil.

The isoscalar giant monopole resonance (ISGMR) in nuclei provides valuable information about the response of the neutron skin, but the strength of the quadrupole and monopole transitions significantly influences experimental results, causing a discrepancy between theory and experiment. This discrepancy is evident in $^{24}$Mg and $^{28}$Si data, so the role of the coupling between the ISGMR and ISQR was investigated to determine its effects on the reduced strength, using coupled cluster theory to calculate both transitions. This coupling was found to reduce the ISGMR strength, but when an adjusted correction was applied, the calculated reduced strength matched the experimental value; adjusting for the transition-coupling effect accurately interprets the data and describes the compact nature of the $^{24}$Mg and $^{28}$Si ISGMR.

Stick-slip movements, characterized by a sudden pause followed by rapid motion, have been observed in various systems including human skeletal muscles and mechanical tools. Researchers from fields like physics, biology, and engineering want to develop models that predict when such movements will occur and how it can be prevented in mechanical systems. However, creating such models proves challenging because they require complex variables to determine whether a pause will happen, which may be impractical in some contexts.

We introduce a mathematical framework to tackle this problem, based on how much force is needed to move an object over different surfaces. This approach considers the importance of slowing down a system in order to overcome friction, which simplifies the conditions needed to predict when a pause will happen. We show mathematically that the likelihood of pause states decreases as the system size decreases, which gives way to stable motion states with preferred velocities. These results have broader applications in understanding the dynamics of systems with resistance to motion.

Reinforcement learning has been plagued by the high variance of policy gradient methods due to Bellman residues.  This variance stems from the combination of model residuals from the dynamics and reward functions that are typically not essential for learning the policy.  In contrast, variance from the dynamics model is necessary for learning, while that from the reward function can be safely eliminated.  Existing literature has addressed the variance introduced by the dynamics model through model-based methods and variance reduction techniques.  We propose a novel approach called Probing Variance Reduction that targets the variance from both the dynamics and reward models simultaneously.  By leveraging a second proximal stochastic gradient descent process, Probing Variance Reduction achieves an optimal trade-off between exploration and variance reduction.  Empirical results on discrete and continuous control benchmarks show significant improvements over prior research, with propragating variance reduction leading to a tenfold reduction in variance, resulting in more consistent training and higher rewards on download and cross downstreamRL libraries.  Code is available at https://github.com/krishna2808/profound-bvr

Incompleteness is a major concern when users provide ratings and recommendations, which are subsequently utilized by content curation and revenue generation systems to make data-driven decisions.  Specifically within recommender systems, users' implicit and explicit interactions often convey a deeper, unspoken purpose which often goes unconsidered during the processing of the received content.  Essentially, users' intentions remain unaccounted for during the content assessment phase, which may result in the rendering of a complete ranking by the system.  Our objective is to uncover the hidden user intent (HU) - which is defined as the desired outcome or content of interest - when users engage with rated content beyond their initial interactions.  A novel framework called HUBER, which is designed to infer users' HU from their sequential data, was developed through a thorough experimentation process.  By applying the framework to various real-world datasets, the results show that the HU clearly represents users' goal or desired content, which is typically distinct from the visited content.  Furthermore, the results indicate that the HU can be accurately inferred from users' interactions with content.  It is our contention that understanding users' hidden intentions is beneficial for system designers to better tailor recommended content to users' needs.

The double confluent Heun equation has limited information in the scientific literature, with only uni-valent solutions described. The present paper aims to derive a general symmetric unfolding of a special form from a known outcome, specifically a uni-valent solution. The process involves transforming the Fuchsian equation into a new form with distinct singular points and determining a meromorphic solution using the monodromy data from an elementary solution. The new solution is a general form that arises from a solvable special case. The paper also illustrates the method with two example cases, demonstrating the effectiveness of the solution generation process. The obtained results can be applied to any uni-valent Fuchsian equation, resulting in a new class of uniformly accessible equations. The method provides a straightforward and efficient solution that can be applied to any equation within the stated class.

The matrix polynomial evaluation under rank-one constraints is a significant problem that has been extensively studied in both theoretical and practical contexts, albeit with little consideration for heterogeneous data. This research addresses this issue by presenting a comprehensive framework for rank-one matrix evaluation with heterogeneity, effectively capturing the characteristics of real-world datasets, which are usually comprised of multiple interconnected subgroups. To establish this framework, we formulate three fundamental requirements that embody the underlying properties of rank-one matrix evaluation with heterogeneity. By demonstrating that these constraints are both necessary and sufficient, we derive a fundamental theorem that provides a standardized solution. Moreover, we illustrate the applicability of our findings through theoretical and empirical examples, which demonstrate that heterogeneous data can be accurately represented by combining subgroups. Additionally, we explore the implications of our research on machine learning.

This paper investigates how three primary sequential elements in sequence can relate to a topological representation. Two key sequential concepts, symmetry and asymmetry, are also introduced and explained. Ultimately, the paper demonstrates the validity of the topological representation under the absence of symmetric elements.

degeneracies in the $b\to s\ell^+\ell^-$ transitions at B-factories. This ratio
equates to the fractional standard model deviation in the $\mathrsfs{R}_{\rm
S{\-}LF{\-}E}{\-}D}{\-}S_{\rm 2d}{\-}S}{\-}2{\-}D}{\-}N}{\-}S}{\-}D}{\-}D$
calculation from non-leptonic $b\to s$ decays. Since theoretical uncertainties
plaguing hadronic decay rates can be mitigated by averaging over different
experimental data sets, this ratio serves as an efficient tool to distinguish

neutral current neutrino mixing. Further, this equatorial symmetry-constrained
combination is valuable for identifying parameters in physics-beyond-the-standard

This research explores the properties of linear multi-channel networks, focusing on their connection to Markovites, a class of multi-variate stochastic processes. It demonstrates that networks featuring certain characteristics, including organized spectra and diagonalizability, belong to the Markovite class. An algorithm is then proposed for the spectral decomposition of such networks via the Kontos algorithm. As an application of this finding, a decentralized control system is developed for these networks, using plug-and-play functionality to incorporate regulation. It is shown that networks featuring certain characteristics, including organized spectra and diagonalizability, can be efficiently regulated via parallel processing and that the Kontos algorithm's properties enable efficient calculation of the algorithm's iterations.

The COVID-19 pandemic has led to a global public health crisis, prompting the development of numerous machine learning models to aid public policy-makers.  There's been ongoing debate about whether to adopt a categorical or continuous approach to predict disease outcomes.  In this paper, a two-phase categorical recommendation model is introduced, which includes the BERT-Disease module to extract relevant disease information and the BERT-Symptom module to assess patient symptoms, and uses their joint features to make a categorical prediction about the likelihood and severity of disease progression.  This model's effectiveness was tested using real data on 8,084 patients from Guangzhou First People's Hospital and on 2,915 patients from Zhongshan Hospital, both part of the Southern Hospital of China.  Experimental results show that the proposed model surpasses existing approaches in both accuracy and performance, setting a new standard for categorical disease prediction.

Network science has become a rapidly evolving field at the intersection of physics, computer science, and sociology due to its versatility in modeling real-world systems. This unification has created a new paradigm for researchers and scientists to approach diverse disciplines beyond natural sciences. However, numerical simulations have replaced theoretical analysis as the primary tool for resolving complex problems in this field. Consequently, a lack of authoritative guidance has led to numerous challenges for early-stage researchers navigating this area. To address this issue, we offer a comprehensive guide tailored for ambitious network researchers, featuring (1) an introduction to fundamental principles and mathematical methodologies; (2) an examination of key analytical and numerical methods, including notable examples and practical applications; (3) an in-depth analysis of the most crucial network parameters and a comparison of popular models, along with relevant references; (4) a detailed explanation of popular network centrality methods and model techniques for important characteristics; (5) an exploration of the interplay between connectivity and node functions, as well as model approaches for modularity and community structure; (6) an analysis of critical vulnerability and key information propagation processes; and (7) an explanation of the most important methods for evaluating model results and fitting parameters. This guide also provides resources for further learning and offers suggestions for aspiring network scientists to engage critically in experimental and theoretical research.

The study of eco-evolutionary dynamics has primarily focused on its rapid and continuous nature, leading to predictions of dramatic and irreversible changes.  However, the early research in this field, including our 2012 work, revealed that evolutionary changes can occur at different speeds and durations - rapid or gradual - and be influenced by various parameters.  Building upon our 2012 research, the current study offers a more comprehensive understanding of eco-evolutionary dynamics, especially in its slower and longer-term aspects.  To achieve this, the theoretical framework for the gradual change was expanded from the previous simple mathematical models to more complex predictions, including theories such as the thermodynamic discussion of dynamic behaviors and mathematical descriptions of dynamic relationships.  Our research shows that gradual changes can occur in response to environmental changes and other factors and that lasting changes, whether rapid or slow, can lead to unpredictable and unusual patterns of behavior among organisms before reaching a state of equilibrium with the environment.  The theories presented in this study provide a more detailed understanding of these phenomena, including the possibility of temporary or permanent changes and the likelihood of temporary or permanent adaptations being realized by a population.

Self-supervised learning methods for speech processing are unique because they don't need labeled data to learn, which is beneficial since labeling speech is a difficult and time-consuming process. However, the speech processing community is still unclear about the nature of the speech representations learned by these models, especially since there are many different types of unsupervised encoders available. To better understand these representations, we have created a new set of benchmarks that evaluate different aspects of unsupervised encoders. Our tests use small, medium, and large models, and assess them on speech, writing, and speech/writing pairs. Our results show that the best encoders, especially the largest ones, can learn speech representations that are compatible with downstream speech processing tasks, but also show that some encoders process writing and speech/writing data differently from pure speech data. This study gives us a better understanding of the trade-offs between improving speech representation models and integrating writing data to enhance our knowledge.

This work offers a detailed examination of blockchain-driven decentralized exchanges. Firstly, we give a thorough understanding of a blockchain exchange's operational process and we classify existing blockchain exchanges into two broad categories, such as centralized blockchain exchanges and decentralized blockchain exchanges. The study then explores the advantages offered by decentralized blockchain exchanges and highlights the potential risks associated with centralized blockchain exchanges. To bridge the existing knowledge gap on decentralized blockchain exchanges, we propose a novel framework known as BlockDEX that offers a comprehensive set of design criteria for evaluating and selecting suitable decentralized blockchain exchanges. The analysis of existing blockchain exchanges against this framework enables us to identify both excellent and inferior decentralized blockchain exchanges. Based on our analysis, we identify key areas that need to be addressed to enhance the quality of decentralized blockchain exchanges and provide recommendations for their improvement. Moreover, we visualize how a decentralized blockchain exchange's functionality can be expanded into a centralized blockchain exchange, promoting a healthy evolution of the ecosystem.

The goal of this study is to introduce a new metric called the'relative sensitivity index' to measure dependence between random variables. This index serves as a version of the 'E-value' tailored for sensitivity analysis and is defined as the ratio of the posterior probability range with missing data to the one without, after adjusting for data gaps. By utilizing the sensitivity index, we can determine the extent to which a model's results rely on specific data points, even in scenarios where those data points are absent or hard to obtain. We create a sensitivity index specific to Bayesian analysis, defined as the ratio of the 95th percentile of the posterior distribution range, calculated using three different data sets, versus the 95th percentile from the prior distribution. We demonstrate the utility of the sensitivity analysis through a binary classification scenario. We also apply this theory to the analysis of existing results from a hydrological study, to illustrate its practical use.

The study of the quantum invariant laurical expansion of a generic linear bundle on the P^1 U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2), considering its symmetry with U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2), is presented. It finds that any quantum invariant linear bundle on the P^1 U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) possesses a unique, symmetric invariant structure with respect to U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2), distinguishing it from the classical case. A comprehensive list of U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)-symmetries for the laurical expansion of any quantum invariant linear bundle on the P^1 U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) is provided, which generalizes the finding in Li (2019). Moreover, a solution to the problem posed by X. Li in arXiv:1902.04252 is provided.

The emergence of Internet of Vehicles technology has brought about a revolution in the way people communicate, offering vast opportunities for enhanced living standards through improved services. To fulfill the ambitious goals of IoT, a robust and open network architecture is necessary, and as a promising solution, the blockchain technology is being considered. In the context of a new data management paradigm driven by distributed ledger technology, secure and efficient data sharing becomes feasible through decentralized, multi-party platforms. In this chapter, a simulation-based federal learning framework for IoT is presented, along with an in-depth literature review of blockchain technology applications in IoT. The discussion covers the challenges associated with implementing federal learning frameworks in IoT, and we offer a concise summary of the survey in conjunction with future directions for future research.

The construction of a superconducting quantum computing hub at the research facility of Fermilab is underway, with the goal of establishing a state-of-the-art temperature control system that can be remotely controlled and maintain temperatures as low as 10 millikelvin. This laboratory, with ample natural neutron flux and sophisticated radiation protection, provides an ideal setting for the intense nuclear reactions necessary for the development of quantum bits using ions and other elements. This document outlines the laboratory's design, with an examination of the procedures in place to ensure the safe operation, supervision, and quality control of the facility, as well as the initial results of the experiments conducted there.

As cryptocurrency adoption grows, so are concerns over its security. Poorly encrypted communication is a common vulnerability that has been exploited numerous times. Our work involves analyzing an unprecedented collection of Python code from the PyPI package repository, focusing on code segments that handle and encrypt cryptocurrency-related data. This study aims to identify and categorize common security breaches in cryptocurrency encryption, which have been previously undocumented. Our research reveals 34 distinct encryption issues, categorizable into five primary groups. It also introduces a new tool to detect the 'SHA256' library, a Python implementation of the SHA-256 hashing algorithm. This tool enables users to scan whether hashed library code matches its original code, helping to prevent hash-based replay attacks. Our research will aid developers in improving the security of their applications by raising awareness of existing issues and recommending preventative measures.

In contemporary urban environments, sound tags play a crucial role in enabling cities to be intelligible to humans and machines alike. They facilitate context-specific retrieval of audiovisual content and serve as essential indicators for emergency response services, all while making cities more accessible to individuals with disabilities. Despite the availability of numerous sound tag datasets, these resources are primarily centered on controlled environments or specialized applications, leaving a significant gap in the development of sound tags for general urban use. To address this knowledge gap, our research leverages an innovative technique involving open-ended real-world polling to create a new large-scale sound tag dataset, which is designed to auto-generate text-based labels based on user descriptions. This polling-based approach is particularly useful for its adaptability to a wide range of domains and objects. The resulting WORTH dataset, comprising audio clips from diverse sources with associated user-generated tags, is a valuable resource for the audio community. To showcase the utility of the WORTH dataset, our research explores two audio classification tasks using this information, highlighting the dataset's ability to support various applications and domains. The WORTH dataset, along with its associated code and polling tools, is made available for public download at https://github.com/PRUS-UC3M/WORTH.

We introduce a novel neural network, the NuSPAN, specifically designed for deconvolving seismic data with a non-uniform sparse model. Unlike conventional seismic inversion methods that treat sparse models as approximation, our model inherently embeds the sparse assumption. The proposed NuSPAN is a proximal network motivated by the dual form of the non-uniform sparse model, and we prove its ability to serve as a surrogate to the sparse model with equal cost function up to a fixed tolerance. The flexibility and adaptability of the NuSPAN make it suitable for various seismic inversion tasks and can also be used in other fields such as astronomy and medical imaging. The effectiveness of the NuSPAN is validated through numerical experiments with synthetic and real-world seismic data, demonstrating its superiority over established models and proximal networks designed for uniform sparsity.

This research investigates the Semigroups of composition operators on specific function spaces, specifically BMOA, BMOA$_0$, and BMOL spaces. These spaces are known for having unique characteristics such as the Bogdan-Stein factorization, preserving properties like the Carleson measure, and being related to the Littlewood subspaces of $H^p$ spaces. By extending and generalizing past theories, including a paper by by R. Z. Chidume et al. on non-compact operations, this study provides novel findings on such operators in these spaces.

A recently developed method for amending linear operators is adapted from wavefunction overlap matrices. We demonstrate that any matrix can be expressed as a combination of positive eigenvalues and roots of unit, and propose a set of positive operators that combine to form any matrix. We provide an alternative proof and show this approach has practical implications by leveraging wavefunction overlap matrices to derive a universal length-independent correction for Haagerup model's ground state computations.

Annotated part-of-speech (POS) labels for written language have become a crucial asset in language technology. However, obtaining these labels is a labor-intensive process, especially for older collections that often contain irregular spelling and grammar. Existing methods rely on decision trees that can produce unreliable outcomes, particularly in the presence of ambiguous texts. This study proposes a novel Set-Valued Machine Learning framework to account for the uncertainty in POS annotation by viewing potential labels as a probability distribution over possible outcomes. A novel preprocessing technique, called Standardization plus Normalization (S+N), is also developed to standardize tokenized texts and represent the uncertainty in historical collections. Additionally, the uncertainty in the training data is modeled using mixed distributions that combine categorical and continuous outcomes. An existing POS model is adapted to work with the proposed distributional framework, allowing for more accurate measures of uncertainty. An evaluation of the model's performance on collections from the 14th to 19th centuries showed that it achieved higher accuracy and better outcome distribution estimates compared to a baseline model based on stochastic grammar analysis. Notably, the accuracy of the adapted model improved by 4.7% or more in some test cases, while its ability to account for uncertainty was confirmed through numerous metrics and user ratings.

This study investigates how certain characteristics of a function with "corners" influence its relationship with its gradient, specifically whether taking these points into consideration can determine the function's components. Two critical parameters - a function's curvature at these points and how its gradient changes there - are found to provide this information, providing a framework for distinguishing between different types of geometric objects, like spheres and paraboloids. Several practical applications of this theory are also discovered, including a method for determining whether a function is differentiable and how to find the closest smooth version of a given function, both from its values alone and with additional constraints. This method can be adapted to different function classes, not just those with sharp corners, and a key property is proven for a specific class of functions, including those with curved edges: the existence of a unique smooth version that replicates these functions' behavior.

An increasing number of businesses are utilizing artificial intelligence services, which generate expectations about how their applications will perform. Decision-makers need to consider these expectations to make informed business decisions, such as deploying AI services. Since various stakeholders, including businesses and citizens, have distinct expectations regarding city operations, these expectations must be formally documented to ensure they are implemented in decision-making processes. Although existing methods for eliciting and managing requirements can be applied to city expectations as well, a new approach is necessary to analyze and validate these expectations aligning with actual outcomes. Our proposal introduces an AI-powered assistant that can translate business expectations into formal specifications by collecting data on historical city operations, capturing the nuances of decision-makers' inputs, and adjusting these inputs if the resulting specifications cannot be fulfilled. Our approach also involves real-time verification to ensure that the translated specifications comply with available resources and existing policies during the data collection process.

A quantum error-corrected circuit is proposed, which incorporates the concealed inverses protocol (CIP) to tackle the issue of incorrect gate usage within the surface code. CIP combines the error-correction capabilities of redundant calculations with a single, merged quantum operation, rather than relying on separate error-detection and correction steps. By simulating this circuit using superconducting quantum systems, the results show that it can reliably execute a three-qubit CNOT operation despite the presence of various hardware errors. Additionally, the surface code's error correction performance in this setup is compared across two different error models, one featuring uniform error rates and another with real-world varying error rates. Within the context of reducing quantum error rates below threshold values, the proposed CIP-based circuit is discussed in relation to its potential applications within the reliable execution of quantum simulations and computations.

The fundamental idea of a preorder can be seen as the union of all equivalence relationships defined within it, and this fact can be more fully understood when considering a preorder as the result of combining two separate categorical structures: one that is equivalent to a set and the other that contains all fully inclusive relations. Theoretically, any regular category can be viewed as having two distinct components - one that facilitates the creation of paths and another that enforces equality among them. The category that enables path creation is essentially a type of category that resembles a line, and its corresponding category that enforces equality enables a unique equivalence relationship that can be applied to any existing path, resulting in an equivalence relationship that can be visualized as a collection of disconnected lines. However, to accurately depict a preorder through path depiction, it's crucial that for any given path there exists another path that may originate at a different point but ultimately converges to the same endpoint. The existence of such a mechanism within a regular category involves modifying the category so paths can be shortened and allows for a unique path equivalence that can serve as an accurate representation of the original preorder. However, our analysis shows that a category that can effectively depict a preorder through path depiction and also support a unique path equivalence cannot be characterized through finite category construction parameters.

To conduct a thorough investigation into the relationship between severe coastal storms and extreme sea level events, we develop a novel statistical model. This new model, designed to handle high-dimensional multivariate data with irregular spatial patterns, is used to identify areas with high concentrations of severe coastal storms while simulating realistic sea level events. Based on a large dataset of severe coastal storms in the UK's eastern coast from 1884 to 1990, we identify areas with increased extreme sea level events and severe coastal storms when compared to random combinations of the two. Our model also discovers significant spatial patterns that could be used to improve the prediction of severe coastal storms and extreme sea level events.

Recently, pre-trained vision-language models have gained significant attention due to their potential in integrating visual and language information to accomplish a variety of tasks. Despite achieving impressive performance with large-scale image-text datasets, they often struggle to understand subtle text cues representing complex visual concepts. To address this limitation, we introduce a technique that employs a dual approach to refine the representation of visual and text information through a two-way pre-training strategy. By incorporating a module that identifies and localizes important visual features in response to challenging words, a vocabulary of visual-only words can learn to capture high-level visual patterns and comprehend complex text references during the word-image matching process. Consequently, our proposed model achieves state-of-the-art performance on various visual reasoning tasks without any fine-tuning, outperforming other prominent vision-language models by a substantial margin. Furthermore, we illustrate the model's capability by visualizing the attention maps of predicted features, demonstrating a more accurate understanding of visual properties.

Quantum technology holds great promise due to its unique state transformations, but real-world applications rely on more complex linear operator matrices performing single-qubit gates along with other operations. To address this, we study the universality of quantum-like operator matrices in processing any linear transformation. Building on a theoretical model of noisy quantum computation, we investigate similar models for matrix systems. To achieve this, we focus on developing target operator matrices starting from a basic switching mechanism. To efficiently generate matrix elements, we introduce a new concept of similarity transformation. The introduced ideas of operator matrices extend existing methods, enabling rapid construction. Furthermore, we reveal that certain restrictions on operator matrices remain insufficient for universality. To improve universality, we propose expanded matrix protocols, introducing new single-qubit gates while maintaining efficiency. Additionally, we clarify the necessary conditions for ideal noisiness in matrix systems, extending existing results from quantum computation. Our findings serve as a foundation for understanding the universality of similar computation models, with far-reaching applications in operator matrix technology.

Given a k-dimensional local ring R with a prime characteristic p, and a k-category T containing the trivial groupideally, we define a sub-set Λ_R of the set of k-dimensional list of integers which satisfies a particular condition related to the prime characteristic p, and the local ring R. This condition is such that if a list of integers belongs to Λ_R, then the sum of each integer and p also belongs to Λ_R. Now, let P and Q be two Hilbert polynomials that are both valid for the given category T, and are both compact in the sense that they belong to the set Λ_R. Under these conditions, we prove that the ring R is F-finite if and only if the difference between P and Q also belongs to the set Λ_R. This result has further implications which lead to an identification of the sets Λ_R for certain types of rings. Specifically, the result holds for Gorenstein rings of codimension d with the characteristic not equal to 2, in which case the set Λ_R consists of the set of all lists of integers from 1 to d+1. This result also holds for 2-categories in the sense of Y. Li's work. In addition to these results, we further demonstrate an improved version of the previous statement by showing that the ring R is actually F-finite if and only if the set of possible values for the polynomials P and Q is the set from 1 to d+1. In the field of computer-aided diagnosis based on imaging, standards such as DICOM allow for standardized image processing and distribution. However, standardized reporting of imaging-based results, including machine learning model outputs and histopathology slide annotations, is often incomplete. As a solution, we developed Highdicom, a Python framework that enables standardized encoding of image labels and model outputs within DICOM headers. Using this framework, we demonstrate how to standardize and enhance reporting in three specific applications: radiology, pathology, and epidermal melanoma segmentation. Highdicom framework is available on GitHub at https://github.com/brasss/highdicom.

We start by using the surface energy density to represent a black hole's horizon energy, and we derive an expression for this energy density in surface energy density, in a form that is consistent with the Einstein-Hilbert action's surface energy density through the application of Noether's charge. This charged density leads to a derivation of Virasoro algebra, and subsequently gives rise to the holographic entanglement entropy formula for black holes. This finding provides new perspective on the structural connection between holography, gauge symmetry, and gravity as suggested by Noether's charge. We further propose that the thermal boundary condition of holography can be formulated by requiring the vanishing of the surface energy density charged by Noether's charge. This formulation has the effect of generating unitary time-evolution for bulk and boundary states. We conclude by employing Noether's charge to investigate the energy density of the Maggiore-Sotlani-Maldacena-Motl black hole.

In the rapidly expanding field of computational molecular biology, effective data analysis is crucial to tackle complex problems, and recent breakthroughs in data visualization using dimensionality reduction have significantly aided this process. Inspired by successful unsupervised learning methods in the general field of machine learning, we have developed an unsupervised approach to embed DNA sequences into a low-dimensional space while preserving key characteristics. Our sequencing-based technique, called SeqView, uses a novel combination of preservers of DNA sequence properties and a state-of-the-art unsupervised learning algorithm, applying a modified version of UMAP to the enhanced representation. By incorporating the chemical structure and other important attributes of DNA sequences, SeqView's embedding more closely represents its intrinsic properties. We have shown that our sequencing-based method outperforms existing approaches in preserving key aspects of DNA sequences. Additionally, we have successfully applied SeqView to the analysis of transposable elements, allowing for the identification of ubiquitous viral insertions in the human genome that were previously overlooked by traditional methods.

V$_2$O$_3$(0001) is a correlated system that transitions between metallic and insulating states in response to doping, with the metallic state being restored through high levels of oxygen incorporation. This is because oxygen overcharging counteracts the metallic state, but the correlation between this process and the film's surface properties remains unexplored. To address this, our study examines how the metallic-insulating transition in V$_2$O$_3$(0001) films is modified when exposed to varying surface characteristics. We utilized a bespoke sample preparation method to obtain high-quality V$_2$O$_3$(0001) films with controlled metallic and insulating properties, as well as altered oxygen levels, in situ X-ray photoemission spectroscopy to analyze the surface composition, and in situ DC oxygen treatment to follow the transformation from metallic to insulating state. Our findings reveal a significant delay in the transition from metallic to insulating state for films with modified surfaces. We attribute this behavior to the enhanced adhesion of oxygen molecules on the surfaces of these films, leading to increased oxygen incorporation and subsequent transition delays. To confirm this, we utilized in situ DC oxygen treatment to replicate the conditions leading to the transition delay for the film with the modified surface, but in this case, it led to the transition delay of a film with the native surface. This reveals that the surface chemistry of V$_2$O$_3$(0001) is intricately tied to its metal-insulator transition

We've developed a universal method to convert any Lie-Poisson equation with a single independent variable into a corresponding Hamiltonian system, using Clebsch variables. This approach works by integrating the original equation and then employing a related momentum map that acts as a generator. We've discovered that the associated Hamiltonian system comprises two parts: one cycle momentum and one additional integrable cycle momentum which also satisfies an related Lie-Poisson equation. This method effectively offers an alternative to using the backward Hamiltonian system and also serves as an update to the Lie-Poisson reduction method originally proposed by Marsden and Ratiu. As demonstration, we've selected four significant Lie-Poisson equations with a single variable and presented their corresponding Hamiltonian systems in phase space.

To broaden our understanding of anomalous planet parameters, our team analyzed 2018 planetary discoveries made by KMTNet in a specific region with better seeing conditions. We identified 25 anomalies, consisting of 11 single planets and 14 multiple planet systems, compared to 20 anomalies found in years with better seeing conditions. Interestingly, our data suggest that prime-field Anomalous Planets lean more towards M dwarfs than expected, but sub-prime Anomets show no such preference. Furthermore, our findings indicate that Anomets show strong lensing signals and have smaller ratios of out-of-plane to in-plane masses than typical planetary microlensing candidates, which may support the planet-mass Anometal hypothesis. We also found no distinct mass anomalies for Anomets compared to typical planetary lenses. The multiple Anomets appear to have a shorter timescale for peak magnification than single Anomets and are more evenly distributed across peaks. The multiple Anomets are less offset in the lens motion, making them more similar to multiple planet lenses than single planet lenses. These results align with the multiple-anomalogous-to-multiple-planets analogy. Last, our data show that Anomets tend to have larger f/b ratios and more positive residuals on the S-bias than planetary lenses, which may support the anomalous planet parameters explanation for the S-bias residual. This is the second part of a series of papers that investigate the development of a novel algorithmic paradigm for addressing inner regions of nonlinear hyperbolic conservation equations. The proposed methodology is based on the pioneering work of Bresin et al. who developed a system of two coupled equations to handle the requirements of both asymptotic and inner domains in a single model. The method is applied to the non-stationary compressible Navier-Stokes equations with isentropic flow in three dimensions, where a composite domain is considered with a general flow in the outer region and rarefied gas in the inner domain. The solution to the inner problem depends on the outer solution but the method doesn't impose flow continuity at the interface due to the nontrivial inner region dynamics. The introduced model consists of two equations: one describing the outer flow and another for the inner region which also introduces new mass sources and sinks to simulate momentum transfer between domains. The method uses a novel approach to solve the inner region problem with no slip condition applied there, unlike traditional models. The method aims to provide a first-order approximation only as higher-order effects are expected to be small in general. The method applies a first-order model only to parts of the domain where the flow is mostly non-trivial. It further uses a simplified first-order model for regions near walls by combining it with well-established methods and concepts for treating these areas. This paper identifies and assesses relevant characteristics for determining whether an object is nuclear power plant material or not, based on a dataset from the International Atomic Energy Agency. It uses feature selection as a tool to evaluate the importance of each feature in classification models. To gain a deeper understanding, the study used Weka software for 11 machine learning algorithms, 4 datasets, and 12% of the full dataset for repeated evaluations. The objective is to provide a comprehensive evaluation of the most effective classification methods and their reliability in distinguishing material types accurately. 

The paper's findings reveal that the Support Vector Machines method exhibited the highest accuracy in identifying material types, with a 99.07% success rate. Notably, our study is the first to analyze feature importance for material type classification using the IAEA's Nuclear Power Plant dataset. As a result, the study is expected to contribute valuable insights for enhancing machine learning algorithms in nuclear power plant settings. 

Beyond its immediate application, our research has significant broader implications. Firstly, our approach provides a framework for evaluating the effectiveness of classification models in diverse scientific domains. Secondly, our analysis can help identify the most relevant features for classification tasks, which is particularly important in areas where feature redundancy, noise, and computation constraints are significant. Lastly, our application of feature selection in bio-medical and nuclear fields adds a new dimension to the growing literature on feature selection as a decision-making aid in scientific disciplines.

The functions $\mathcal{B}_{n,\lambda}$ are connected to q-rook theory and symmetric functions via de Bruijn panels and Dyck trails. The latter involves the use of colorful Sumbination functions $\mathrm{Sum}_{\lambda}$ which reduce to building-and-dwelling functions $\mathcal{B}_{n,\lambda}$ in a specific case. This approach enables the mapping of partitions $\lambda$ to pairs $(\mu, \kappa)$ consisting of partitions $\mu$ and a composition $\kappa$, by counting boxes $\mathcal{B}_{n,\lambda}(i,j)$ which corresponds to the movement of a q-rook in a $q$-dairy with dimensions $n\times (q+n)$ from position $(i, j)$ to the bottom left corner of the board. The result is a set of discrete, translation-invariant points on the Schur root system graph connecting all partition pairs $(\mu, \kappa)$ of the same weight. Furthermore, it is proven that symmetric functions $\mathrm{Sum}_{\lambda}$ for all partition $\lambda$ form a basis for the space of Dyck trail symmetric functions of dimension $n$. The primary objective of this work is to adapt convolutional neural networks for orientation-independent image classification tasks. Convolutional neural networks are inherently suitable for horizontal image datasets but may not perform well with vertical images, depending on the specific architecture. This issue can be resolved by incorporating various techniques to achieve orientation independence, which have been explored in our research. Our studies revealed that specific layer groups are responsible for this orientation dependence and demonstrated that a particular configuration of these groups is effective in making the network orientation-independent. To validate the effectiveness of our approach, we used the orientation independence metric to evaluate it on a significant dataset and compared it to existing methods.

A general approach has been developed for constructing finite fields of dimensions that are a product of two prime numbers greater than 2, by introducing a unique representation based on unique unitary transformations of $\mathbb{F}_{q^k}$, where $q$ is a power of a prime number, and $k$ is a positive integer. This representation is further linked to specific sets of subspaces within a curved linear interval, which in turn is a specific type of curved space. Additionally, this approach leads to a novel equation involving traces, specifically the relative trace equation, that connects the traces of linear maps across different curved linear intervals.

The variation in parton distribution functions with flavor $n$ depends heavily on the mass of the top quark.  This significant impact of the top quark's mass on the parton distribution functions inspires further investigation into the top quark's contribution to these functions, particularly at high masses.  To better understand the top quark's influence, the analytical framework established in arXiv:2108.02655 is adopted here to examine the top quark's partial PDFs in the context of heavy top masses.  This work primarily focuses on the physical implications of the top quark's role in the parton distribution functions at high masses, particularly for the $n=5$ case, although predictions are also provided for lower flavors up to $n=3$.  This investigation aims to identify the practical significance of potential discrepancies between PDF sets, particularly in regions where the predicted cross sections exhibit significant variation with flavor.

A graph $G$ is given along with its vertex coloring using $k$ distinct colors, denoted as $k$-ACV of $G$. Here, the term 'ACV' stands for 'Arrow's Coloring of Vertices'. Now, considering an edge of $G$ whose endpoints have different colorings, it is said to be properly colored in relation to the given $k$-ACV of $G$. A sequence of properly colored edges is known as a consecutive sequence of proper edges. Graph $G$ is said to have the property of having an invariant number of $n$ consecutive proper edges if for every $k$-ACV of $G$, there exists an $n$ number of consecutive proper edges. In this paper, the author proves that for a given integer $k \geq 2$, if $G$ has its maximum degree less than $k + 1$ and its PMI greater than $2.5$, then $G$ has the property of having an invariant number of consecutive proper edges for every $k$-ACV of $G$. Furthermore, the author proves that such graphs $G$ which satisfy this condition and have a number of vertices greater than or equal to $2k + 3$, are two-edge-tinted graphs. We prove hypercontractive inequality for linear operators acting on modified Bergman spaces, which have the scaling property, and we further extend D. Wittsten's findings to obtain inequality variants for these spaces. In a more exploratory aspect, our study extends the space of Hilbert-Schmidt operators on the unit disk to a broader range of lattices.

The ongoing COVID-19 pandemic has led nations to issue strict surveillance measures, and research is underway to develop accurate detection methods using computed tomography scans, specifically for identifying pulmonary abnormalities. Although previous studies employed three-dimensional image segmentation techniques, they are hampered by low accuracy and efficiency due to the resulting increased dimensionality. To overcome this limitation, this research proposes a two-stage approach using a tailorable neural network architecture that is well-suited for processing multi-channel images and is enhanced with capsule networks to improve low-level pulmonary detail recognition. The framework's initial stage localizes pulmonary regions, whereas the second stage precisely segments the lung fields. The framework exhibited exceptional performance on test images from multiple institutions, yielding AUC scores of 0.962 for detection and 0.986 for segmentation. Furthermore, this method yields outstanding results with only 192 x 192 pixel data from high-resolution CT scans, thereby enabling more efficient processing of large-scale data sets. The framework's technical innovations enable the successful implementation of pulmonary physicians, thereby facilitating clinical diagnosis.

In the past ten years, there has been a significant surge in technological advancements, business innovations, and space policy shifts that have created an unprecedented atmosphere of excitement and investment within the space sector.  As a result, numerous companies, governments, and research organizations are now actively working in low-Earth orbit (LEO) to develop orbital services, including construction jobs, commercial applications, and testing opportunities for space technologies. 

In response to this emerging environment in LEO, various players are exploring innovative uses of space and space technology, driving growth and growth prospects through new business opportunities and revenue streams.  To better understand and navigate this rapidly evolving landscape in LEO, a comprehensive approach is essential – one that considers technological, economic, social, and governance aspects as interconnected components of innovative space business models.

In this book, we take a step-back to analyze LEO from a high-level perspective, focusing on space utilization as the primary framework.  Through this approach, we look at the key players in the LEO ecosystem, consisting of companies, research organizations, governments, and individuals, as well as the various groups that are driving innovation in LEO, including startups, businesses, space organizations, and scientific communities.

By taking a space utilization perspective, we are better equipped to address the diverse set of stakeholders in the LEO ecosystem, identifying their unique objectives and goals. To refine computer-simulated models, especially in structural analysis and fluid dynamics, researchers use finite element methods. These techniques demand high-quality meshes, which must encompass the original object's geometric details. In the past, mesh generation algorithms often failed to produce optimal results, leading to a significant limitation of current methods. In this research, a new optimization-based approach is introduced to create high-order quadrilateral meshes within complex shapes. First, the algorithm identifies a coarse mesh by linking domains of a function that represents a partition. It then utilizes specialized data structures to ensure the quality of the resulting mesh by limiting the angles between its quadrilateral cells. Using a linear optimization problem with whole number solutions, the algorithm finds an optimal partition that satisfies these conditions. In addition to producing high-order meshes, the algorithm is compatible with various geometric shapes, including those with multiple materials and complex sub-domains. It is demonstrated using 2D and 3D examples that this method outperforms and improves upon existing mesh generation algorithms.

The sample correlation coefficient is a widely used measure of linear association between two random variables. In the context of a dataset, this measure can be computed on various subgroupings of the data, known as arrangements. This study develops a comprehensive set of formulas to calculate the expected values and variances of the sample correlation coefficient for any given arrangement of data. These formulas are versatile and can be applied to any type of random variables, including normal distributions. They serve as a basis for a broader theorem and are relevant in four distinct scenarios. In addition, the study provides analytical expressions for the moment ratios that are useful in hypothesis testing and confidence interval constructions for the population correlation coefficient. Furthermore, the research computes the fourth moment of the sample correlation coefficient for non-parametric arrangements, enabling simulations to be conducted.
We detail the scattering matrix formulation of the quantum theory of general relativity and explore its potential extensions into the quantum field theory and black holes of any dimension.

We study three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations in a periodic box. It's well-known that mild solutions to these equations can be found in the class of Leray-Hopf operators when initial conditions are in $H^1$. However, these solutions fail to be $C$-continuous with respect to the initial condition in this space. To address this issue, we establish that it's possible to create a feedback operator that is finite-dimensional and locally distributed within the interior that stabilizes the Navier-Stakes equations when the initial conditions are in the space. To achieve this, we work with a closed and convex set of potentially large $L^q$-norm bounded functions in addition to moments and strain measures. This allows us to create a feedback operator that is continuous with respect to the $L^q$-norm and then extend this work to the context of Besov spaces using a suitably chosen function that is in $L^q$. The final result simplifies to uniform stabilization in the $H^1$-norm when $q = 1$ and to uniform stabilization in the sense of Strichartz representation when $q = 2$.

The LitMind Lexicon is a comprehensive dictionary of contemporary Chinese that is informed by real-world usage and can be accessed online for free. This multivalent dictionary showcases words in context by grouping related entries and displaying examples from relevant contexts, such as synonyms, antonyms, definitions, usage notes and mind-related examples. Examples in the Lexicon are derived from a diverse set of digital sources including news articles, books, user-generated content, social media, online dictionaries and wikis. By synthesizing data from these various sources, the Lexicon offers a more complete picture of Chinese language and culture than traditional datasets and has the added benefit of allowing users to query and seed standardization for words and phrases of interest.

Understanding why a recommended item was chosen is an important issue, particularly where issues of fairness and transparency arise.  From a technical standpoint, deciphering explanations is complicated by the interpretative model's lack of consideration for time series data's inherent temporal nature, which makes accurate descriptions challenging.  Furthermore, precise explanations that clearly identify item attributes may not be feasible, leaving models to make concessions in accuracy in order to enhance interpretability.  From a more human-centered viewpoint, individuals' varied levels of technical proficiency may render elaborate explanations useless, making simplicity and clarity essential considerations.  This research addresses these concerns by adapting a time series analysis method specifically for use in Recommendation Systems, incorporating a new module that controls the balance between accuracy and interpretability.  Results from our human subject study indicate that this trade-off between these variables can be viewed as a multi-dimensional problem, with participants' preferences falling along different dimensions.  Ultimately, our research demonstrates the potential of our model across multiple dimensions and provides a first-hand analysis of the efficacy of LIME-RS.

Indium arsenide quantum wells are considered a viable alternative to traditional gallium arsenide quantum dots for the generation of energy harvestable solar energy. They have the potential to be integrated into the surface of silicon solar cells through the incorporation of a silicon layer within its structure. However, our computational investigation indicates that this integration leads to the generation of electronic traps adjacent to the quantum well. These surface electronic traps are known to impede the efficient transfer of electrons. We have demonstrated that our findings can be further optimized by introducing a very thin layer separating the quantum well from the silicon layer. This optimization reduces the elevation of the quantum well's energy level, decreases the density of electronic traps, and modifies the character of the traps, both of which are essential criteria for achieving maximum energy efficiency within the solar cell.

In deep neural networks, ensemble learning often achieves improved generalization by combining multiple models' predictions. However, when dealing with costly models or time-sensitive scenarios like autonomous driving, this can significantly increase inference time, making ensemble learning impractical. To address this issue, we can replace the traditional ensemble of local models with a single, higher-level neural network that uses regional queries. These regional queries essentially act as simplified sub-networks within the main model, allowing for efficient learning and prediction. Through theoretical analysis and experiments, we have found that regional queries in a hierarchical network can lead to comparable performance and added benefits of stability and robustness. Specifically, bymerging these regional models into a unified network, we have achieved (1) a 90% reduction in inference time, (2) a modest improvement in test accuracy, (3) increased model robustness, and (4) enhanced adversarial robustness. Moreover, regional queries' ability to enhance generalization and resilience when trained with adversarial methods or augmentations demonstrates their utility in scenarios involving corruption and the importance of efficient learning.

Our previous research successfully reduced the time complexity of the sinkhorn algorithm from O(n^2) to O(n) by introducing a novel column-wise kernel filter. In this paper, we introduce two cutting-edge linear-time cotree structures: the diagonal block kernel filter and the linear block kernel filter. The former enables us to utilize a diagonal-based filtering approach, transforming the sinkhorn algorithm's floating point operations from O(n^2) to O(n). We have also derived a precise integer-based optimal transport solution, building upon our previous integer relative scaling concept. This novel approach not only eliminates floating point operations but also yields a highly efficient solution algorithm with a linear time complexity, especially suitable for computing the sinkhorn matrix of large datasets quickly.

Our research involves analyzing FUV observations of AU Mic that were taken over a five-year period with IUVWS on Kepler, a wide-field telescope. Most of these observations showed the system in a quiescent state but also captured two planets orbiting within the debris disk in tandem with intense star eruptions. Both planets influence the surrounding disk's morphology and emissions. Kepler observations confirm AU Mic b, with its mass estimated to be around 0.08 Jupiter mass, is tidally locked and has a longer orbital period than previously estimated. Moreover, our findings support the existence of a previously unknown planet, AU Mic c, with a mass similar to that of Neptune, located at a distance of approximately 8-10 astronomical units from its parent star. This planet's discovery is supported by variations in FUV emissions that cannot be attributed to either AU Mic a or b, suggesting it plays a significant role in shaping the debris disk's structure and emissions. Moreover, our analysis shows that planets in AU Mic system dominate its reprocessing of the energy released from its parent star into the surrounding debris disk, contrasting with the Jupiter-Moon system. While both systems share debris disk properties, AU Mic c's discovery indicates its debris disk has a higher level of dynamism and tidal forces than initially thought, which could have a profound impact on any potential exoplanets within the system, including AU Mic c and b.
